title: Digital Anaesthesia Patient Education and Acceptance
summary:
Patient satisfaction is an important parameter for recording how patients rate the care provided. By systematically recording this, we can improve the quality of our care and adapt our services more individually to the needs of patients.
This is a study that is only being conducted at the University Medical Centre Mannheim. The study is being carried out in various surgical areas. A total of 750 patients will be surveyed over a period of 3 months. In addition, all participating doctors (approx. 40 people) will be interviewed.
The user experience of patients and doctors will then be analysed. This includes satisfaction with the solution, suggestions for improvement or gaps in data collection. The time spent in the consultation and the consistency of the data recorded by the software with the data recorded in the doctor-patient consultation are also analysed.
We are conducting this study in accordance with the internationally recognised guideline, the WMA Declaration of Helsinki, and are complying with the Data Protection Act. The responsible ethics committee has reviewed and evaluated the research project.
Procedure:
Following the personal information session with the anaesthetist, patients are asked whether they would like to take part in our study. If they decide to take part in the study, they have to answer a questionnaire with a total of 10 questions, which takes around 4 minutes. It is possible to complete this questionnaire directly on site in paper form, alternatively you can also complete the questionnaire digitally at a later date.
If you decide not to take part in the study, there are no disadvantages for you. The decision also has no influence on medical care.

interventions.name: Once the indication for surgery has been established, patients are given access to pre-operative screening software. This replaces the paper-based pre-operative questioning. The software is an approved medical device that is regularly used in the Department of Anaesthesiology at the University Medic

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
o ASA classification I-IV
o Patients from the following departments: Clinic for Urology and Urosurgery, Clinic for Gynaecology, Surgical Clinic: Rectal Centre, Bariatric Surgery
o Signed declaration of consent for participation in the study)
Exclusion criteria:
o Emergency interventions
o < 18 years of age
o Mental impairment that does not allow the patient to understand the nature, scope and significance of the research project
